meta.document: RETENTION_POLICY_SCHEDULE — machine-readable personal-data retention policy schedule
meta.adr: ADR-005_RETENTION_VS_IMMUTABLE_AUDIT.md (PROPOSED — operator-ruled mechanism; this schedule carries the numbers)
meta.scheduleRequirement: ADR-005 'Retention schedule requirement' paragraph — binding on the V1CAP-066 contract

validationGate.gate: V1-minimal gate per ADR-005: every personal-data-bearing record family in recordFamilyInventory must reference a policy ID that resolves to a matching policy entry (same recordFamily and dataClassification). A family without a resolvable policy reference is a validation FAILURE (exit 1).
validationGate.determinism: offline and deterministic — no database, no network, no wall-clock inputs

provenance.method: Record families enumerated by inspection of database/supabase/migrations/*.sql (CREATE TABLE statements) and frontend/src/lib/ contracts; every family cites the migration files that create its tables.
provenance.durationStatus: All retention durations and expiry triggers are PROVISIONAL DEFAULTS. ADR-005 UNKNOWNs rule that concrete durations are jurisdiction-dependent (education records, child data, staff payroll) and require operator/legal input; this schedule carries explicit defaults so the gate is enforceable now and is expected to be re-ruled by the operator without changing the mechanism.
provenance.crossTenantErasure: ADR-005 UNKNOWN: whether a subject spanning multiple tenants is erased per-tenant or globally is unresolved (COND-003 tenant_id type ruling); every policy here is scoped per tenant class and erasure scope is recorded in the erasure event (ADR-005 reconciliation mechanism).

reconciliationModel.mechanism: ADR-005 Option 2 — redaction-with-tombstone is the V1 erasure mechanism. Immutable records are never mutated or deleted; erasure appends an erasure event referencing the tombstoned record IDs, the retention policy ID, the authorizing identity, and the erasure scope.
reconciliationModel.erasureEvent: append-only audit event; itself a record of the audit family
reconciliationModel.verificationInvariant: for every tombstoned record: the record exists, is non-readable as personal data through the redaction layer, and its erasure event is present and well-formed
reconciliationModel.neverForgotten: decision facts (event type, tenant attribution, timestamp/ordering, actor role and relationship structure, policy reference), verification results, evidence-class metadata, and the erasure event itself
reconciliationModel.forgotten: subject-identifying personal values inside audit/event/memory/evidence records, memory-store personal content, AI snapshot personal content, personal identifiers in knowledge-graph personal nodes

dataClassification.notes: public/internal/restricted mirror the context-assembly sensitivity vocabulary (cg_memory_record.sensitivity). 'personal' marks families carrying subject-identifying values. 'special-category' marks biometric and equivalent highly-sensitive classes (Constitution §19 minimization applies maximally). Data classification is a Prime Directive input (AGENTS Prime Directive §6).

tenantClass.notes: Every request carries tenant context (AGENTS §13). 'platform' denotes the Control Plane (AGENTS §14) — it is NOT a tenant, but platform-operated records still require a retention ruling.

retentionKind.notes: ADR-005: 'retention duration or event-triggered expiry'. event-triggered entries carry a named trigger and an optional maxRetentionDays backstop.

lawfulBasis.notes: Lawful basis per record family and tenant class; special-category processing (biometrics) requires explicit-consent.

erasureMechanism.notes: tombstone is the ADR-005 Option 2 default (redaction-with-tombstone; immutable records are never mutated or deleted). crypto-shred is Option 1 and is ONLY valid where the schedule designates a shred-class; no family is designated in V1 — crypto-shredding is deferred to a follow-up ADR unless the operator designates a data class (ADR-005 implementation path step 5).

retention.notes: AI snapshots are redacted per the AI privacy pipeline; retention aligned to V1CAP-066 (shortest window in the schedule — child and student prompt/response content).

erasure.redactionPlaceholder: record erased per retention policy RP-AISNAP-EDU

downstreamAggregation.obligation: Only operational aggregates (token counts, latency distributions, success rates) survive expiry; personal conversation content is never aggregated into any downstream surface (AGENTS §19 minimization).

erasure.redactionPlaceholder: record erased per retention policy RP-AISNAP-ORG

downstreamAggregation.obligation: Only operational aggregates survive expiry; personal conversation content is never aggregated downstream.

retention.notes: Child/education-record retention runs to the end of the institutional relationship plus the statutory window; the number is a provisional default pending operator/legal ruling (ADR-005 UNKNOWN).

erasure.redactionPlaceholder: record erased per retention policy RP-IDPRO-EDU

downstreamAggregation.obligation: Enrollment/headcount statistics may survive erasure as aggregates; aggregates are Intelligence, never Reality.

erasure.scope: subject-identifying profile values
erasure.redactionPlaceholder: record erased per retention policy RP-IDPRO-ORG

downstreamAggregation.obligation: Membership/headcount statistics may survive erasure as aggregates.

retention.notes: Special-category data: minimization is maximal (AGENTS §19); erasure on consent withdrawal is immediate regardless of the backstop. cryptoShredCandidate = true: whether biometric references become a designated crypto-shred class depends on COND-009 (legacy durable-tables disposition) and an explicit operator designation — until then the tombstone mechanism applies (ADR-005 implementation path step 5).

erasure.scope: biometric reference material (face_template_hash and any derived template); enrollment audit facts (who, when, under which policy) are retained
erasure.redactionPlaceholder: record erased per retention policy RP-BIOMET-EDU

downstreamAggregation.obligation: No biometric-derived aggregates are permitted downstream; only verification outcome counts (non-biometric operational statistics) may be aggregated.

retention.notes: Employment/payroll records typically carry statutory retention obligations (tax, labor law); the 7-year backstop is a provisional default pending operator/legal ruling.

erasure.scope: personal values in employment, payroll, leave, discipline, and clinic records where the lawful basis has expired; statutory-obligation fields are retained for the statutory period and take precedence
erasure.redactionPlaceholder: record erased per retention policy RP-WKFOR-EDU

downstreamAggregation.obligation: Workforce analytics aggregate over positions and periods; aggregates are Intelligence, never Reality.

erasure.scope: personal values in employment and position records where the lawful basis has expired
erasure.redactionPlaceholder: record erased per retention policy RP-WKFOR-ORG

downstreamAggregation.obligation: Workforce analytics aggregate over positions and periods.

retention.notes: Activity/behavioral records of minors (attendance, study sessions, hostel, library, content reads) carry a short window and mandatory aggregation.

erasure.redactionPlaceholder: record erased per retention policy RP-ATTND-EDU

erasure.redactionPlaceholder: record erased per retention policy RP-ATTND-ORG

recordFamilyInventory.description: Append-only audit and access records: memory access audits, execution history, verification results, platform audit logs, and attendance verification logs. Decision facts, tenant attribution, provenance, and the erasure events themselves are never forgotten (ADR-005 'What may NOT be forgotten').
personalValues: attendance verification subject and device context
recordFamilyInventory.tombstoneInvariant: immutable — erasure appends an erasure event and tombstones personal values through the redaction layer; the record row is never mutated or deleted (AGENTS §28; ADR-005 Option 2).

recordFamilyInventory.description: Append-only event fabric and operational event logs. cg_event is append-only by design (V1CAP-041) and already matches the tombstone model.
personalValues: free-text event payloads containing personal content
recordFamilyInventory.tombstoneInvariant: immutable — tombstoned, never deleted; event type, tenant attribution, timestamp, and policy reference survive erasure in full.

recordFamilyInventory.description: Durable practical/organizational memory tier and kernel observations. Platform-owned data, never agent-owned (G-061). Purpose-limited per AGENTS §19: expired purpose means redaction.
recordFamilyInventory.tombstoneInvariant: immutable with append-only supersession — erasure tombstones personal content; the record row and its envelope/provenance are never mutated or deleted.

recordFamilyInventory.description: Foundation evidence artifacts produced by the verification pipeline. Evidence-class metadata (what was verified, when, under which policy) is never forgotten (ADR-005).
personalValues: personal content embedded in evidence artifacts and payloads
recordFamilyInventory.tombstoneInvariant: immutable — erasure tombstones embedded personal content; verification results and evidence-class metadata are retained in full.

recordFamilyInventory.description: AI interaction snapshots: conversations and prompt/response interaction logs. Redacted per the AI privacy pipeline; retention aligned to V1CAP-066 (AGENTS §19/§21).
recordFamilyInventory.tombstoneInvariant: not an immutable audit family, but erasure still uses the tombstone mechanism for uniformity: personal content is redacted through the projection layer and the erasure event is appended; rows are never silently deleted.

recordFamilyInventory.description: Subject master data: identities, user/student/staff profiles, guardian mappings, admissions, and membership records. The canonical Reality layer for who a subject is within a tenant.
recordFamilyInventory.tombstoneInvariant: profile correction is via supersession/status; erasure tombstones subject-identifying values and appends the erasure event — no destructive deletion.

recordFamilyInventory.description: Biometric enrollment references (legacy scholar substrate). Special-category data; maximal minimization. cryptoShredCandidate — designation depends on COND-009 and an explicit operator ruling; tombstone applies until then.
personalValues: face_template_hash and any derived biometric template
recordFamilyInventory.tombstoneInvariant: erasure tombstones the biometric reference and appends the erasure event; enrollment audit facts survive. Crypto-shred becomes the mechanism ONLY on explicit operator designation recorded in a follow-up ADR.

recordFamilyInventory.description: Employment, payroll, leave, discipline, and clinic records plus the governed workforce position substrate.
recordFamilyInventory.tombstoneInvariant: erasure tombstones personal values after the lawful basis/statutory period expires; statutory-obligation fields take precedence and are retained for the statutory period.

recordFamilyInventory.description: Individual attendance and engagement/activity records of subjects, including minors' activity traces (study sessions, hostel attendance, library borrowings, content reads).
personalValues: activity traces tied to a minor or adult subject
recordFamilyInventory.tombstoneInvariant: erasure tombstones subject-identifying values once the retention window passes AND the mandatory downstream aggregation has produced the surviving statistics (aggregates are Intelligence, never Reality).

recordFamilyInventory.description: Fee, subscription, and ledger records. Payment-security facts (signature validation, idempotency, replay-protection records) are audit facts and never erased (AGENTS §36).
recordFamilyInventory.tombstoneInvariant: legal-obligation retention takes precedence over erasure for the statutory period; after expiry, subject-identifying values are tombstoned and transaction facts survive.

recordFamilyInventory.description: Messages, notifications, and notification preferences tied to subjects.
recordFamilyInventory.tombstoneInvariant: erasure tombstones message/payload content; delivery audit facts survive.

recordFamilyInventory.description: Generic CoreObject envelopes (cg_entity, cg_relationship): free-form payloads that MAY carry personal values. Declared personal-data-bearing conservatively (Prime Directive: data classification is an input; unknown payload shape must fail safe).
personalValues: subject-identifying values inside generic CoreObject payloads
recordFamilyInventory.tombstoneInvariant: immutable with bi-temporal supersession — erasure tombstones payload personal values; envelope, provenance, and decision facts survive.

recordFamilyInventory.description: Tenant, scope, role, worker-definition, mission, geofence, and platform configuration records that carry NO subject-identifying personal values by design (identities are referenced, never embedded).
recordFamilyInventory.tombstoneInvariant: not personal-data-bearing: no erasure policy required. If any of these tables later gains a personal-data column, it MUST be re-declared into a personal-data-bearing family (the gate fails an undeclared family only when it is declared PDB without a policy — so re-declaration is the author's duty, AGENTS §12 provenance).

summary.gate: every personalDataBearing family references a resolvable policyId — enforced by scripts/verify-retention-schedule.mjs (exit 1 on failure)
